title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page restarts and cleans up the setup drafted on the previous page. It is the preamble to a standard 'presentation of an extension' lemma for groupoids. Data: (1) a morphism of groupoids p: T̃ → T. (2) A family of arrows (ũ_i)_{i∈I} in T̃. (3) Their images (u_i) in T, assumed to generate T. Grothendieck notes in parentheses that generation implies Ob T consists of the sources and targets of the u_i, so every object is reached. One then chooses defining relations of T on these generators. To encode words with inverses he takes (4) I' = I × {±1} and sets (5) u'_{(i,ε)} = u_i^ε. A relation is an element of the free 'word set' (6) Î' = ∐_{n∈N*} I'^n. Each relation index α∈A thus gives a length n_α and a word (i'_{α,1},…,i'_{α,n_α}). The next page requires the corresponding arrows of T to be composable and to form a loop, and imposes M_α(u)=1. The continuation (next page) lifts each relator to T̃, where the lifted arrows ũ' need no longer be composable. It then introduces fibre arrows a_j (arrows projecting to identities) to fill the gaps, together with fibre relations S_β (previous page). The aim is evidently a presentation of T̃ by generators ũ_i and a_j, with relations of three kinds: lifted relators corrected by fibre words, the fibre relations, and conjugation of fibre arrows by the ũ_i. This is the groupoid version of P. Hall's presentation of a group extension N → G̃ → G. In the Teichmüller-groupoid context it serves to bootstrap presentations of the T_{g,ν} along 'fibration' morphisms such as forgetting a marked point or a boundary. These are Birman-exact-sequence-type steps, as used in the standard approach to presentations of mapping class groups and of the Teichmüller tower in the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor point: generation by the u_i only forces every object of T to be a source or target of some u_i when T has no isolated objects with trivial automorphisms. Grothendieck's parenthetical is a harmless convention, presupposing connected components that are not reduced to bare points.

ideas.what: Encoding a presentation of a groupoid by generators, signed indices I×{±1}, and relators as words in ∐_n I'^n that are composable loops
ideas.modern_name: presentation of a groupoid (free groupoid on a graph modulo relators)
ideas.where_published: Implicitly in Esquisse d'un programme (presentations of the Teichmüller tower by generators and relations in genus 0 and 1)

ideas.what: Presenting an extension groupoid T̃ → T from a presentation of T plus generators and relations for the fibre arrows (setup only on this page)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard setup for presenting a groupoid extension. It is useful context for how Grothendieck intended to derive presentations of Teichmüller groupoids, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: The equation label for Î' = ∐_{n∈N*} I'^n is (6), not (8); the next page continues with (7).
